label: Self-created technical demo — not client work
title: Search and status filters silently ignored (stale derived state)
summary: In a small React checklist app, the search box and the status filter looked broken: typing or picking a status changed nothing on screen. The filtered list was kept in its own useState and refreshed by a useEffect that only watched the task array, so it never re-ran when the query or the status changed.
symptom: You type "redirect" into the search box and all nine tasks stay on screen; you click the "Open" filter and the done tasks stay too. The summary line still says "Showing 9 of 9 tasks". As soon as you tick any checkbox, the list suddenly applies the filters you chose earlier, which makes the bug look intermittent and hard to describe.
reproSteps: Check out the bug commit: git checkout demo-bug (then npm install if you have not already).
Start the app: npm run dev, and open the printed localhost URL in a browser.

Type "redirect" in the "Search tasks" box. Expected: only "Configure Supabase auth redirect URL for the production domain" remains. Actual: all 9 tasks stay visible and the summary still reads "Showing 9 of 9 tasks (6 open)".
Click the "Open" status chip. Expected: the 3 done tasks disappear. Actual: nothing changes.
Tick any task checkbox. Actual: the list now suddenly applies both filters, because toggling changes the task array, which is the only thing the effect watches.
Optional: run npm run lint on this commit. ESLint reports react-hooks/exhaustive-deps on the useEffect in src/App.tsx, naming the missing "query" and "status" dependencies.
Return to the fixed code with git checkout main and repeat steps 2 to 4: filtering now happens as you type and as you click.
rootCause: src/App.tsx stored the filtered list as separate state, const [visible, setVisible] = useState<Task[]>(tasks), and synchronised it with useEffect(() => { setVisible(filterTasks(tasks, query, status)) }, [tasks]). The dependency array lists only tasks, so React re-runs the effect when a task is toggled but not when query or status change. The inputs themselves render correctly because they have their own state, so the UI looks responsive while the list silently shows stale data. The react-hooks/exhaustive-deps lint rule flagged exactly this line in the first commit, but a warning is easy to scroll past.
fix: Replace the state-plus-effect pair with a derived value: const visible = useMemo(() => filterTasks(tasks, query, status), [tasks, query, status]). The filtered list is now computed during render from its three inputs, so there is no second copy of the data that can fall out of sync and no extra render pass after each change. The commit also adds a regression test (src/App.test.tsx) that drives the real UI with Testing Library: it types into the search box and selects the Open filter, then asserts on the rendered titles. Unit tests for the pure filterTasks helper (src/lib/filterTasks.test.ts) pin down the matching rules.
lesson: If a value can be computed from props or state, compute it during render (a plain expression or useMemo) instead of copying it into state and syncing it with an effect. Treat react-hooks/exhaustive-deps warnings as bugs until proven otherwise, and cover the user-visible behaviour with a test that fails before the fix.

fix.message: Fix: search and status filters ignored (stale derived state)

images.title: Before the fix: "redirect" typed, nothing filtered
images.alt: The Launch Checklist app at the demo-bug commit with "redirect" typed in the search box: all nine tasks are still listed and the summary reads "Showing 9 of 9 tasks (6 open)".
images.caption: Before the fix. "redirect" has been typed into the search box, yet all 9 tasks are still listed and the summary still says 9 of 9.

images.title: Before the fix: one checkbox ticked, the stale filter suddenly applies
images.alt: The same app after ticking the checkbox of "Configure Supabase auth redirect URL for the production domain": only that task is listed, struck through, and the summary reads "Showing 1 of 9 tasks (5 open)".
images.caption: Still before the fix. Ticking one checkbox changes the task array, the effect finally re-runs, and the list suddenly applies the search typed earlier. This is what made the bug look intermittent.

images.title: After the fix: the same keystrokes filter as you type
images.alt: The fixed app with "redirect" typed in the search box: only "Configure Supabase auth redirect URL for the production domain" is listed and the summary reads "Showing 1 of 9 tasks (6 open)".
images.caption: After the fix. The same keystrokes narrow the list as you type: 1 of 9 tasks shown, no checkbox touched.
